 Judgment
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 27-01-2023 at about 8-00 p.m., the petitioner and his friend Lokanath as a pedestrian were proceeding towards Heggondanahalli from Ramanayakanahalli by walk on the footpath.

At that time the driver of van bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MY-9341 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner from behind,
result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately,
the petitioner was shifted to Balaji Hospital, Bangalore wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to St.John's Medical hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient from 27-01-2023 to 05-02-2023.
So far, petitioner has spent Rs,3,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was doing tent and shamiyana decorative work and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.

Due to the accidental injuries,
petitioner has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - the R.C. owner of Van bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MY-9341 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.

5. The Respondent no.2/the insurer of Van bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MY-9341 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the insured vehicle was not involved in the accident, that the petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gain and that there is a delay of 3 days in lodging the complaint and that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.
6. It is further contended that the petitioner has settled the claim with the owner of the vehicle and the owner has admitted to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Accordingly the petitioner has requested the police to close the case.
In that regard, the investigating officer has filed B report stating that the complaint is closed.

The respondent no.2 has further contended that the driver of Tilak.S vs Muniraju on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41503701/
2
the insured vehicle was not holding a valid driving license.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

Based on the pleadings, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 27-01-2023 at about 8-00 pm., at Ramanayakanahalli village,
Sarjapura Hobli, Bangalore District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Van bearing Reg.No.KA- 03-MY-9341?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3
. What order or Award ?
9. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and three witnesses are examined as PW.2 to PW.4 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P17.
On the other hand, the respondent no.2 examined its official as RW.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.
Dr. Srinivas -MRO at Balaji Nursing Home, Varthur is examined as RW.2 and got marked OPD as Ex.R3.

Shivalingaiah K - Retired ASI, Kaji Somenahalli is examined as RW.3 and got marked FIR as Ex.R4.
10.
Issue No.1:-

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 27-01-2023 at about 8-00 p.m., when the petitioner and his friend Lokanath as a pedestrian were proceeding towards Heggondanahalli from Ramanayakanahalli by walk on the footpath.

At that time the driver of Van bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MY- 9341 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner from behind, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
12.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, charge sheet, etc.,
Tilak.S vs Muniraju on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41503701/
3 13.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sushila case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0023/2023 by Sarjapura Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC and u/Sec. 187 of MV Act.

After completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC and Sec.187 of MV Act.
14. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 at first has disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident on the ground of delay in lodging the complaint.

Further they have disputed the very maintainability of the petition on the ground that petitioner has already settled the matter with the owner of the offending vehicle by receiving compensation from the owner out of court,
hence only Investigation Officer has filed B report before the Jurisdictional Court and hence petitioner cannot be permitted to get double compensation through the present petition.
The learned counsel in further has disputed the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle as the sole cause for the accident.

15. In the light of the aforesaid objection raised by the respondent no.2, if the police records and the evidence of PW1 to PW.4 and the evidence of RW.1 to RW. 3 are perused, it is true that accident in question has occurred on 27-01-2023 at 8-00 pm., and complaint came to be lodged on 30-01-2023 and there is delay of 3 days in lodging the complaint.
In the complaint the reason for delay has been explained stating that complainant being the mother of the petitioner was engaged in attending the petitioner in the hospital.
If the medical records are perused, from 27-01-2023 till 05-02- 2023 petitioner was taking treatment at St.John Hospital as inpatient.
Further if the medical records are perused, on the date of accident itself without any delay petitioner was shifted to Balaji Hospital and from there he was shifted to St.John Hospital.
In the hospital records, the history of Accident is mentioned as "RTA, four wheeler hit to the pedestrian (ie.) petitioner".
Hence, there is every reason to believe that offending vehicle was involved in the accident and the petitioner has assigned valid reason for delay in lodging the complainant.

If really offending vehicle was not involved in the accident, the respondent no.2 could not raise the defence that the owner of the offending vehicle had settled the amount to the petitioner towards compensation.
If really offending vehicle was not involved, question of giving compensation by the owner of the offending vehicle as stated by the respondent no.2 does not arise.
Hence, involvement of offending vehicle is proved by the petitioner.

16. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, except the complaint, FIR and the oral evidence of PW.1, there is no other evidence to prove the aforesaid material issue.
It is true that investigation officer has filed final B report.

As per the case of respondent no.2, since the petitioner has settled the matter amicably with the owner of the offending vehicle, by receiving compensation amount from the owner, they have not co-opeated to the investigation of the case and in view of the statement given by the complainant and injured person to the effect that they have received amount from the owner of the offending vehicle, towards the expenses incurred by them and that they do not wish to continue the case, the I.O without proceeding with the investigation filed Final "B" report before the court.

It is the evidence of the investigating officer (ie) RW.3 that though he had given two notices to the complainant to co-operate in conducting the spot mahazar and though he had given one more notice to keep the eye witnesses present but the petitioner and his family members did not co-operate by not presenting Tilak.
S vs Muniraju

on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41503701/
4 the witnesses instead the complainant by appearing before the investigating Officer, given statement that since they have received compensation amount from the owner of the offending vehicle and since they find it difficult to wander to the court in conducting the case, to close the case.
Based on the statement of the complainant they filed B report to the court.

Hence, RW.3 could not proceed with the investigating and not collected document pertaining to the offending vehicle and not drawn the spot mahazar, sketch etc.,
17.

It is relevant to state here that the owner of the offending vehicle who was arrayed as respondent no.1 in the present case has not contested the case and thereby not disputed either the involvement of offending vehicle or the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle in causing the accident.

Further if really the accident in question was not due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, question of the owner of offending vehicle coming forward for the alleged settlement does not arise.
As per the case of respondent no.2, since the owner of the offending vehicle compensated the petitioner, the petitioner has not proceeded with the police case.

Hence, if the defence of the respondent no.2 is accepted as true for the sake of discussion, then without the offending vehicle being involved in the accident and without the driver of the offending vehicle being the cause for the accident, there is no even remote possibility of their agreeing for settlement.

Hence, even though there is no spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report etc., to prove the issue no.1, but the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the Ex.P1 and the very defence of the respondent no.2 would suffice to hold that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
18

. Now the defence taken by the respondent no.2 as to the compensation received by the petitioner from the respondent no.1 out of court much prior to the filing of the claim petition is concerned, the RW.3 who is the investigation Officer in his evidence has stated that based on the statement given by the complainant (PW.2) and based on the statement given by the injured person (ie) petitioner and one Lokanath by admitting the compensation received by them from the respondent no.1, he has closed the case by filing the B report to the court.

Hence the statement allegedly given by the complainant, petitioner and Lokanath before the investigating officer during the course of investigation is a vital document to prove the defence of the respondent no.2.
But the respondent no.2 having marked B report as Ex.R4 through RW.3, not produced the statement allegedly given by the complainant, petitioner and Lokanath.

The statement allegedly given by the complainant,
petitioner, and Lokanath plays very important role in the present case.
Unless the said document is produced, there is no reason to accept the version of the respondent no.2.

Further the respondent no.2 having taken the defence that the respondent no.1- the RC owner of the offending vehicle had settled the matter by paying compensation to the petitioner, but respondent no.2 has not taken any such contention.

The respondent no.2 could have examined the respondent no.1 in support of their case and could have elicited from the mouth of respondent no.1 of any amount by way of compensation given by him to the petitioner.
As per the own evidence of RW.3 ie., Investigating Officer, the owner of the offending vehicle had not given the amount to the petitioner in his presence.
Based on the alleged statement given by PW.1 and PW.2 he has filed 'B' report.
But as observed supra no statement allegedly given by PW.1 and PW.2 is produced before the court.
Further RW.1 the official of respondent no.2 company having taken such defence, not in a position to state for how much amount case was settled.
There is no iota of document to prove the settlement Tilak.

on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41503701/
5 of amount.
The PW.1 and PW.2 have clearly denied any amount received by them from the respondent no.1 towards the settlement.
19. As per Ex.P1, case was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle u/Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.

The medical document discloses that the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries (ie.,)
grievous injuries which attract offence u/Sec. 338 of IPC.
20.
Usually B report is filed when the police find no evidence or the case is found to be false or mistaken.

If the injured person has received money and no longer wishes to pursue the case, they can inform the court while the police cannot close a non compoundable case as Sec.279 IPC is a non compoundable offence and if a settlement is reached, the parties should file a petition for compounding if offence is compoundable and if necessary approach the Hon'ble High Court u/Sec.
482 Cr.PC to quash the proceedings.
Hence, the I.O is not permitted to file B report only on the ground that petitioner has received the amount from the owner of the offending vehicle.

Hence,
RW.3 has not conducted the investigation properly.

21. Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the judgment relied by the learned counsel for petitioner reported in ILR 1996 KAR 161 between Meenakshamma Vs. Hanumanthappa wherein it was held that "The claim is summary civil proceeding wherein the claimant is required to prove the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle by independent evidence.

Hence, non registration of a police case regarding the accident does not give rise to any adverse inference that no such Motor accident occurred".
22.
In the said case no complaint was lodged regarding accident.
In spite of that compensation was awarded to the petitioner.

23. But in the present case, complaint was filed, investigation was conducted in part, but even in non compoundable offence I.O filed B report not on the ground that no evidence was found or case was found to be false but on the ground that parties have settled the case.

But as there is no material placed on record to prove the settlement of amount outside the court between the petitioner and respondent no.1, it cannot be said that the present claim petition is not maintainable.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
24. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., discharge summary which is marked at Ex.P3.
On going through the medical document it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at ST John's Medical College Hospital as an inpatient from 29-01-2023 to 05- 02-2023 for a period of 7 days.
The petitioner has sustained Left shaft of femur fracture.
The petitioner has not produced wound certificate.
25. Dr. S A Somashekara - Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore is examined as PW.3 and through him OPD book and x-ray film are marked as Ex.P11 and Ex.P12.
PW.3 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 11-11-2024 clinically, rediological for assessment of disability.

PW.3 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent disability of left lower limb Tilak.S vs Muniraju on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41503701/
6 at 39% and on whole body at 19% and that the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.40,000/- in a private set up.
26.
If the cross examination of PW.3 is perused, at first PW.3 has not given treatment to the petitioner at any stage.
Further having assessed the disability on particular limb at 39%, the Pw.3 has assessed the disability on whole body at 19%.

As per judgment reported in 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki,
Taluk the normal rule would be disability in the lower limb would be 1/3 rd of the particular limb.

sentences.text:
Hence, this court inclines to consider the disability of petitioner on whole body at 13%.
27.
Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
28. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained grievous injury.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering.

29. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced 16 medical bills for Rs.67,628/- as per Ex.P7, Inpatient bill as per Ex.P13 for Rs.98,707/- and outpatient bill for Rs. 4,070/- and pharmacy bill for Rs.2,409/-.
30.
To evidence the fact that the family of the petitioner had paid the bill amount, the petitioner has examined his mother as PW.2.

PW.2 has deposed that on 28-01-2023 the owner cum driver of the offending vehicle namely Muniraju came to hospital and requested her not to lodge any complaint pertaining to the accident and agreed to pay the entire hospital, medical bills and compensation.
Thereafter, he took U turn and neither visited the hospital nor paid the hospital expenses and compensation.
PW.2 and her son have not received any amount from the 1st respondent and they have paid entire hospital bills.

31. If the evidence of PW4 is perused, he has admitted that pharmacy bills are included in the final bill and the medical expenses are not reimbursed and that the medical bills produced by the petitioner are duplicate bills.

32. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has vehemently argued that since medical expenses were met by the owner of the offending vehicle the petitioner could not produce the original medical bills.

33. If the argument canvassed by the Learned counsel for respondent no.2 is accepted as true then the medical bills would have been in the name of respondent no.1 and it would have been in the custody of respondent no.1 and respondent no.1 would have appeared before the court and would have pleaded before the court about the medical expenses met by him.

Hence, this court inclines to award compensation under the medical expenses to the tune of Rs.1,05,186/- (98,707 + Rs.4070+
Rs. 2409).

As pharmacy bills are included in the final bill as evident from the evidence of PW.4 and Tilak.S vs Muniraju on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41503701/
7
final bill this court declines to consider the Pharmacy bill produced by the petitioner.
34. It is stated that petitioner was aged about 19 years and he was doing Tent and Shamiyana decorative work and was earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, year of accident and the place of residence considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.16,000/- p.m.
35.
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and has taken treatment for 7 days as inpatient in ST John's Medical College Hospital, Bangalore.

sentences.text: Hence the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of two months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during the laid down period as Rs.16,000/- p.m., for two months.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.32,000/-
(16,000x2) towards loss of income during the laid down period .
36. From the evidence of PW.1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at ST John's Medical College Hospital, Bangalore.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further for 7 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.

Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.20,000/-
taking into consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2023.
37.
The petitioner has contended that, he was aged about 19 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P6/Aadhar card of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 07-04-2004, that means he was aged about 19 years.
Hence considering the copy of Aadhaar card this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 19 years at the time of accident.

38. So taking into consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.16,000/- p.m and by considering the evidence of PW.3 as he has assessed disability on higher side, this court inclines to take the disability on whole body at 13% and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 19 years, as per Sarla Varma's case, the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 is '18'.
So by applying the multiplier '18' the future loss of income due to disability would comes to Rs.4,49,280/- (i.e., Rs.16,000 x13% x 18 x 12).
Hence this Tribunal holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,49,280/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
39. So far as the future medical expense is concerned, even though PW.3 has deposed that petitioner needs removal of implant which costs approximately Rs.40,000/-, but he has not given any estimation
. Hence, this court awards compensation under the head future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.20,000/-.

8 40.
The petitioner at his age of 19 years has suffered permanent disability, hence definitely some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities would have caused to the petitioner.
Hence he is entitled for sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomfort.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.7,51,466/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Fifty One Thousand Four Hundred Sixty Six only).
30
As regarding liability is concerned, respondent no.1 is the RC owner and respondent no.2 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered.
31. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,51,466/- cost of Rs.1500/- imposed vide order on IA No.II.

opennyai_summary.facts: This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 27-01-2023 at about 8-00 pm., at Ramanayakanahalli village,
Sarjapura Hobli, Bangalore District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Van bearing Reg.No.KA- 03-MY-9341?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3
. What order or Award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sushila case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0023/2023 by Sarjapura Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC and u/Sec. 187 of MV Act.
After completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC and Sec.187 of MV Act.
Hence, there is every reason to believe that offending vehicle was involved in the accident and the petitioner has assigned valid reason for delay in lodging the complainant.
If really offending vehicle was not involved in the accident, the respondent no.2 could not raise the defence that the owner of the offending vehicle had settled the amount to the petitioner towards compensation.
If really offending vehicle was not involved, question of giving compensation by the owner of the offending vehicle as stated by the respondent no.2 does not arise.
Hence, involvement of offending vehicle is proved by the petitioner.
As per the case of respondent no.2, since the petitioner has settled the matter amicably with the owner of the offending vehicle, by receiving compensation amount from the owner, they have not co-opeated to the investigation of the case and in view of the statement given by the complainant and injured person to the effect that they have received amount from the owner of the offending vehicle, towards the expenses incurred by them and that they do not wish to continue the case, the I.O without proceeding with the investigation filed Final "B" report before the court.
It is the evidence of the investigating officer (ie) RW.3 that though he had given two notices to the complainant to co-operate in conducting the spot mahazar and though he had given one more notice to keep the eye witnesses present but the petitioner and his family members did not co-operate by not presenting Tilak.
As per the case of respondent no.2, since the owner of the offending vehicle compensated the petitioner, the petitioner has not proceeded with the police case.
Hence, if the defence of the respondent no.2 is accepted as true for the sake of discussion, then without the offending vehicle being involved in the accident and without the driver of the offending vehicle being the cause for the accident, there is no even remote possibility of their agreeing for settlement.
Hence, even though there is no spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report etc., to prove the issue no.1, but the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the Ex.P1 and the very defence of the respondent no.2 would suffice to hold that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
18
Hence the statement allegedly given by the complainant, petitioner and Lokanath before the investigating officer during the course of investigation is a vital document to prove the defence of the respondent no.2.
But the respondent no.2 having marked B report as Ex.R4 through RW.3, not produced the statement allegedly given by the complainant, petitioner and Lokanath.
Further the respondent no.2 having taken the defence that the respondent no.1- the RC owner of the offending vehicle had settled the matter by paying compensation to the petitioner, but respondent no.2 has not taken any such contention.
Usually B report is filed when the police find no evidence or the case is found to be false or mistaken.
If the injured person has received money and no longer wishes to pursue the case, they can inform the court while the police cannot close a non compoundable case as Sec.279 IPC is a non compoundable offence and if a settlement is reached, the parties should file a petition for compounding if offence is compoundable and if necessary approach the Hon'ble High Court u/Sec.
482 Cr.PC to quash the proceedings.
Hence, the I.O is not permitted to file B report only on the ground that petitioner has received the amount from the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence,
RW.3 has not conducted the investigation properly.
But as there is no material placed on record to prove the settlement of amount outside the court between the petitioner and respondent no.1, it cannot be said that the present claim petition is not maintainable.
Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
28. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained grievous injury.
Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering.
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and has taken treatment for 7 days as inpatient in ST John's Medical College Hospital, Bangalore.
Hence the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of two months as complete laid down period.
Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during the laid down period as Rs.16,000/- p.m., for two months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.32,000/-
(16,000x2) towards loss of income during the laid down period .

. Hence, this court awards compensation under the head future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.20,000/-.

31. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,51,466/- cost of Rs.1500/- imposed vide order on IA No.II.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.7,52,966/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Fifty Two Thousand Nine Hundred Sixty Six only).
Tilak.
A Sum of Rs.7,31,466/-shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit. .
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
